subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt/rebase the open fork PR, replace it with a fresh narrow same-repo fix, or close that branch before queueing another fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug boundary is clear, but an open conflicting fork PR still uses closing syntax and is not a clean landing path, so automation should pause until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.

options.title: Adopt Or Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the fork PR to current main, add missing current-path coverage and proof, then review it as the landing candidate.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the existing fork PR even though it is conflicting, not maintainer-modifiable, and has not updated since April 28, 2026.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the original session-picker work and has the clearest recent routing signal in the same title-precedence area.
